title: consent-driven-redaction-for-scheduled-usage-exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers have asked for stronger guarantees that scheduled usage exports (CSV/Parquet and webhook deliveries) do not leak personally-identifiable or consent-revoked data. Today our scheduled exporters apply static column-level redaction rules at export time, but that model fails when a user revokes consent between the export generation and delivery window or when tenant-specific consent rules vary across accounts.

Goal: Implement a consent-driven redaction layer for scheduled exports that: 1) captures a consent snapshot at export generation time, 2) supports post-generation consent revocation semantics (either pause/delay delivery or remove/redact affected records before delivery), 3) provides an interactive export-preview in the console showing redacted fields for that tenant, and 4) emits auditable events and manifests to support customer audits and forensics.

Success metrics: 
- No high-severity customer complaints about exported PII within 90 days of launch.
- 99.9% of scheduled exports complete without manual intervention; consent-related delays tracked and retriable.
- Console preview accuracy >= 99% compared to final export output in production tests.

Scope & deliverables: 
- Consent snapshot service (lightweight per-export read of tenant consent rules).
- Streaming redaction transform integrated into exporter pipeline (S3/HTTP webhook exporters) that can apply masking, pseudonymization, or removal policies per-record.
- Delivery policy options: "deliver-as-generated" (explicit snapshot applied), "hold-on-revocation" (delay delivery and notify tenant admin), and "post-process-redact" (attempt to redact and re-emit).
- Console UI preview endpoint + preview generation job for on-demand validation.
- Audit manifest format change to include consent_snapshot_id and redaction_summary.

Constraints and assumptions: 
- We cannot guarantee recall of exported bytes already delivered to external SFTP/HTTP endpoints; legal/contractual work required for true revocation after delivery.
- Exporter throughput must degrade minimally; transforms should be capable of streaming per-row with backpressure.

Open questions: 
- Default behavior for tenants that opt-out of holding deliveries on revocation: deliver-as-generated or reject export?
- How to surface consent rule conflicts between organization-level policy and per-user preferences?

Risks: 
- Performance regression on large multi-GB exports if redaction is implemented as a batch transform. Mitigation: implement streaming stateful transforms with bounded memory.
- Increased operational complexity for exported manifests and replay logic. Mitigation: standardize manifest fields and add compatibility versioning.

comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha: Completed spike — consent snapshot model stored as small immutable JSON blob with id and policy version. PoC shows snapshot read is <5ms for typical tenant.

2025-01-20 - Diego: Implemented streaming transformer prototype. Observed ~18% CPU increase for exporter worker under synthetic load; switching to a bounded worker pool and native mask kernels to reduce overhead.
2025-01-28 - PM (Claire Huang): Request to add tenant-level admin control for delivery policy. Added to scope; may impact rollout plan.
2025-02-02 - Security review note (S. O'Neill): Require that consent_snapshot_id is included in audit logs and manifests; flagged retention policy for snapshots (retain 2 years).

2025-02-08 - QA (Ravi Patel): Integration tests failing intermittently when export contains nested JSON columns — root cause: current CSV serializer flattens inconsistent schemas; solution: normalize schema at transform boundary. Assigned ENG-221340 to follow up.

2025-02-11 - Legal (Marta Svensson): Concern about handling consent revocation after external delivery. Suggested default behavior for "hold-on-revocation" and customer opt-in for post-processing redaction. Legal review required before enabling post-process-redact by default.

2025-02-12 - Diego: Merged PR for consent snapshot service (GH #5823). Next: implement manifest changes and preview endpoint. Noted a follow-up to benchmark S3 multipart streaming with transform in path.
release_notes: Adds consent snapshot support, streaming redaction layer for scheduled exports, audit manifest additions, and a console preview endpoint (feature gated per-tenant).
notes_for_oncall: If exporters start logging redaction-failure events, alert on >5/minute sustained rate. Use dashboard exports/consent-redaction/alerts for triage.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: consent snapshot service + streaming transform in beta for small tenants. Phase 2: console preview and audit manifest rollout. Phase 3: opt-in post-process redaction and wider enablement.
customer_comms: Draft email template and console banner prepared in Confluence. Coordinate with Growth and Support for staged rollout to beta customers.
legal_hold_behavior: Exports under legal hold bypass delivery hold but include redaction_summary in manifest; retention of snapshots extended to align with hold duration.
